speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly where the pain and weakness are located, and do they radiate down into your fingers? Please rate your pain level from 1 to 10.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the one-year duration and specific progression suggest a compressive neuropathy rather than acute trauma. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, do you notice any numbness in the "ring" and "little" fingers of both hands, or is it more uniform across all digits? Also, does turning your head to the side or extending your neck make the pain and numbness significantly worse?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with concurrent Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy. The combination of progressive upper and lower motor neuron signs (fasciculations and absent reflexes) in a patient with neck and arm pain strongly suggests ALS, though the specific distribution warrants ruling out compressive myelopathy. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Cervical Spine. REQUEST TEST: EMG/NCS.
